title: Deep learning, deeper relief: pipeline toward tailored analgesia for experimental animal models.
authors: Barleben, Luisa; Simon, Mareike; Drees, Lisa; Flohr, Franziska; Jochum, Christoph; Di Virgilio, Michela; Tacke, Frank; Broer, Sonja; Wolf, Jana; Kolesnichenko, Marina
one_liner_zh: 该文用深度学习语言模型筛选镇痛药以减少对NF-kB转录因子活性的干扰，虽涉及转录因子但非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，方法亦非针对TF-DNA结合预测或分子模拟，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Effective pain management in animal models is crucial for maintaining ethical and scientific integrity. However, commonly used analgesics may affect immune responses and disturb signaling pathways, thereby potentially confounding the experimental outcomes. In mouse colitis models, opioids and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs have been shown to interfere with the immune response and the activation of the central regulator of inflammation, the transcription factor nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappaB). Here, we propose a tailored pipeline for the identification and the validation of analgesics with minimal off-target effects. This approach combines protein-centered relation extraction using deep language models and distant supervision via the Protein-Centered Association Extraction with Deep Language (PEDL(+)) together with an in vivo experimental validation with a NF-kappaB reporter mouse model that enables unambiguous visualization of direct NF-kappaB activity across different tissues. Our findings indicate that commonly used analgesics, such as tramadol and acetaminophen, not only interfere with immune cell recruitment and NF-kappaB activation but also skew the differentiation of epithelial stem cells into goblet cells, affecting epithelial functions even after short exposures. Conversely, the analgesics selected by our PEDL(+)-based workflow, such as piritramide, demonstrated no significant interference with NF-kappaB signaling. To validate our findings in vivo, we treated our NF-kappaB reporter mice with the analgesics selected by our computational pipeline. Amantadine demonstrated the least impact on the inflammatory responses and NF-kappaB activation. We then predicted and identified the signaling pathways that are impacted by amantadine treatment. In summary, our proposed pipeline facilitates a shift from one-size-fits-all analgesics to a precision medicine approach that considers the unique molecular interactions associated with each model.
abstract_zh: 在动物模型中有效的疼痛管理对于维护伦理和科学完整性至关重要。然而，常用的镇痛药可能影响免疫反应并干扰信号通路，从而可能混淆实验结果。在小鼠结肠炎模型中，阿片类药物和非甾体抗炎药已被证明会干扰免疫反应以及炎症核心调节因子——转录因子核因子κB（NF-kappaB）的激活。在此，我们提出了一种定制化流程，用于识别和验证具有最小脱靶效应的镇痛药。该方法结合了基于蛋白质中心的关系提取（利用深度语言模型和通过蛋白质中心关联提取与深度语言（PEDL(+)）的远距离监督），以及使用NF-kappaB报告基因小鼠模型进行的体内实验验证，该模型能够无歧义地可视化不同组织中直接的NF-kappaB活性。我们的研究结果表明，常用镇痛药，如曲马多和对乙酰氨基酚，不仅干扰免疫细胞募集和NF-kappaB激活，还会使上皮干细胞的分化偏向杯状细胞，即使在短期暴露后也影响上皮功能。相反，我们基于PEDL(+)流程选择的镇痛药，如哌替啶，显示出对NF-kappaB信号无显著干扰。为了在体内验证我们的发现，我们用计算流程选择的镇痛药处理了NF-kappaB报告基因小鼠。金刚烷胺对炎症反应和NF-kappaB激活的影响最小。随后，我们预测并识别了受金刚烷胺处理影响的信号通路。总之，我们提出的流程促进了从一刀切式镇痛药向考虑每个模型独特分子相互作用的精准医学方法的转变。
